summary: The shallow half of a deliberate shallow-vs-deep comparison of embedding Cooper's TTR in Coq (companion: TTR_theorems_deep.v). Renders a toy TTR fragment natively: ptypes as Ind -> Prop predicates, record types as Coq Records (ManRuns, ManWalks, IndOnly), width subtyping as hand-written coercions, meet/join as /\ and \/, singleton subtyping as equality rewriting. Part A proves six parallel toy theorems (every-man-runs inference, width subtyping, meet/join subtype laws, singleton, transitivity); Part B shows where shallow is cleaner (dependent record inference, native existentials, compile-time safety); Part C documents in prose six things the shallow embedding CANNOT do: types as values (universe collapse), computing a merge of record types, generic relabelling (only a hand-written isomorphism, proved as a roundtrip), proving a type empty, cross-model reasoning (no model parameter), and dynamic type construction from runtime data. The file's real content is Part C: it is a diagnosis of where TTR's type-as-value core resists a shallow Coq rendering.

sources.citation: Cooper, R. (2005). Records and record types in semantic theory. Journal of Logic and Computation 15(2):99-112.
Cooper, R. (2012). Type theory and semantics in flux. In Handbook of the Philosophy of Science 14: Philosophy of Linguistics, 271-323.
Cooper, R., Dobnik, S., Lappin, S. & Larsson, S. (2015). Probabilistic type theory and natural language semantics. LiLT 10 — adjacent (probabilistic TTR), not the fragment formalized here.

evidence: All 12 theorems end in Qed; the only global assumptions are 9 signature Parameters (one Set, one constant, six predicates) with no propositional content, so Print Assumptions stays within rubric section 3(a); the 4 Hypotheses are section-local and discharge into theorem premises.

Core TTR definitions are changed by the shallow rendering: record types become native Coq Records with fixed projections, meet/join become /\ and \/ on Prop, subtyping becomes per-pair coercion functions — each alters which claims are provable, and the file says so explicitly.

Part C (lines 172-278) is the file's own admission that TTR headline machinery — types as values (C1), record-type merge (C2), generic relabelling (C3), empty-type reasoning (C4), cross-model reasoning (C5), dynamic type construction (C6) — cannot be stated in this embedding at all.

What is proved is honest but toy-scale: application, and/or intro-elim, rewriting, one record construction and one hand-written isomorphism roundtrip; several would be excluded as trivial by a rubric section 3 verifier.

determination_rationale: Judged from this file alone, TTR under a shallow Coq embedding cannot keep its core definitions: record types, meet/join, and subtyping all had to be changed, and the operations that make TTR distinctive (merge, relabelling, types-as-values, dynamic type construction) are documented in Part C as unrepresentable — the file's own conclusion is that recovering them requires re-founding the formalization as a deep embedding (the TTR_theorems_deep.v companion). That is the rubric's section 4 criterion 3 pattern exactly: only a partial formalization exists, and headline machinery is recoverable only after restructuring. The Part C diagnosis is genuine evidence about the theory — TTR's identification of types with values is a class (ii) collision with Coq's universe discipline, not a mere engineering gap.

artifact_classes.description: TTR treats types as first-class values; a record field of type Set forces the record into Type (C1), and types cannot be computed from runtime values (C6) — the shallow embedding hits the type-value collapse directly and documents it

missing native structure: Coq has no operation producing a new Record type by merging two others (C2) and no generic relabelling — labels are not first-class, so isomorphisms must be written by hand per pair (C3); no model parameter for cross-model reasoning (C5); width subtyping needs hand-declared coercions

notes: Record produced by the batch audit sweep of 2026-09-05; pre-atlas pilot file predating the zero-axiom discipline (9 global Parameters, all signature-only, so propositional_axioms = 0; section Hypotheses discharge into theorem premises). Its value is comparative-methodological (Part C diagnosis) rather than source-coverage; no specific TTR text is cited and no core TTR paper is on disk under papers/.
